newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IOC, Petronas in refinery talks.
newsitem.headline: India's IOC, Petronas in refinery talks.

text.p: Malaysia's state-owned oil refiner Petronas and Indian Oil Corp (IOC) are discussing plans to build a refinery and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) import and storage facilities in India, a senior Petronas official said on Wednesday.

"Petronas has recently signed a memorandum of collaboration with state-owned Indian Oil Corp to undertake various oil related business projects for mutual benefit," Amyn Mohammed Hussain, Petronas' senior manager for refining and marketing, told an oil and gas conference in the Indian capital.

"Currently, we are discussing plans to build a refinery at Nagapattinam on India's southeast coast," Hussain said on the last day of the two-day meeting, organised by an independent think tank, the Tata Energy Research Institute.
Hussain said the production capacity and configuration of the refinery have not been finalised but output was expected to be about 130,000 barrels per day.
Expected to be operational early in the next decade, the plant will look to service markets both domestically and in the nations around the Indian Ocean, he said.
"The parties are also undertaking to build refrigerated LPG import and storage facilities with a capacity of 30,000 tonnes at Calcutta, in eastern India," Hussain said.
He said the setting up of similar facilities in the southeastern coast of India was also on the drawing board.

"Petronas is already discussing the opportunities to participate either in supplying the LNG or in building the required regasification facilities and LNG terminals, building gas-fired power plants as well as pipeline laying and construction in various parts of India," Hussain said.
He hoped India would keep up the momentum in implementing full market reforms and further liberalise its policies, taxation structure and investment incentives to remain globally competitive.
